body:
I don't think overwriting the existing behaviour makes sense. That would make behaviours unlike all other registry based things which all ignore duplicate object definitions.

Throwing an error might work but may make registries awkward to work with.
Overwriting the config is probably the best option we have here, but any change we make should be applied consistently to components, helpers and tasks.

So you would say this is an expected behavior here? Then there is no real good/DRY way to dynamically overwrite as you would always have to start checking for existing behaviors first then.
If I intentionally (re)add a behavior, I would expect it to force-overwrite. Otherwise I would have taken the overhead of conditional checks or tried to write to config() only. It also makes upgrading from 2.x more difficult where this was just the thing that happened ;)

In 2.x behaviors were completely unlike helpers and components - which always ignored duplicate assignments. I tried to make behavior configuration match the other extension points as it was the odd duck out.

I'm OK with updating loaded modules with new runtime configuration if they already exist. I think this would satisfy your root problem. It doesn't fix any issues that may arise from additional __construct() behavior that should be acted upon by the behavior's configuration though.

I think it should maybe throw an exception if you try to configure the behavior twice. To me, that signals that the developer isn't aware of previous behavior, and thus might end up having confusing configuration set at different points in their app.

If you do it in the right place, e.g, initialize(), it is prior to any events triggered, if I got that right, so overwriting settings of existing should work good across behaviors, components, helpers. 

That way you can do general setup and have some more specific setup in some places.

I think having that flexibility is more important than newbie/developer guarding in this case.

Should the config then be merged rather that overwritten?
I'm with @josegonzalez on this, throwing an exception is what makes more sense. If you want to change a behavior config, and it allows you to change it, you should use its config() method.

Does config() allow merge vs reset/overwrite?
Then I agree. Otherwise it should reset with addBehavior(). And merge will be done using config().
If there is another way to reconfigure, throwing an exception is just fine.
@dereuromark Yes all the config() methods provide overwrite/merge options.
How frequently do you actually reconfigure/redeclare attached behaviors? Right now it is two method calls which doesn't seem excessive for a less frequently done task.

As mentioned above this will be problematic mainly for upgrading 2.x stuff. As it introduces an issue where there wasn't and doesn't need to be one. Other than that the test cases mainly do that a lot.
So having 100 lines extra doesnt sound too compelling to me either :)

Just want to point out that it would be easily solvable at this point using a reset here.
But if you feel like this should throw an exception instead I am fine with it too.
The only clean way in that case would be removeBehavior() (conditional check for existence included?) + addBehavior(), though, for the above reasons.
Do your behavior test cases rely on models already having behaviors attached?

:+1: for throwing an exception. `add`ing should do what is says.

If you want to overwrite, add a special method yourself or may be we should provide one in the core.
This could be a method that quite a few devs want to implement anyway...
